reply_text:
I reviewed `excerpt-helper` against `main` (2 commits) and wouldn't merge it yet. Its one excerpt test passes, but when I tried more cases, short previews are wrong in two ways.

**Must fix**

1. **Every excerpt gets an ellipsis, even when nothing was cut.** `excerpt()` always adds `…`. So `excerpt('hi', 10)` gives `"hi…"`, and an empty body gives `"…"`. The README says text at or under the limit comes back unchanged, and that the ellipsis only appears when text was removed. The code needs to return the trimmed text early when `trimmed.length <= limit`.

2. **A word ending exactly at the limit gets dropped.** `lastSpaceBefore` uses `text.slice(0, limit)`, so it never looks at the character at the limit. So `excerpt('the quick brown', 9)` gives `"the…"` instead of `"the quick…"`, which breaks the README's "at or before the limit" rule. It should also check whether `text[limit]` is a space.

**Should fix**

3. **`toPlain` removes underscores and tildes from normal text.** The regex `[*_~`]` turns `my_var_name` into `myvarname`, which matters for a snippet app.
4. **`toPlain` only handles some markdown.** Headings, list markers and images aren't handled: `'# Title\n- ![img](x.png)'` becomes `"# Title - !img"`. Either handle these or make the README less broad than "markers removed".
5. **The tests miss the cases above.** Please add tests for: text under the limit, text exactly at the limit, a word ending at the limit, an empty string, and a word longer than the limit with no spaces.

**Minor**

6. **The changelog's 1.4.0 entry was also changed** ("a title and a body" → "title and body"). It's probably accidental, and past entries should usually stay as released.
7. **Excerpts can be one character longer than `limit`,** because the ellipsis comes after the cut. That's fine if you meant it, but worth noting in the README.

The version bump to 1.5.0 and the new changelog entry look right. I didn't change anything on the branch.
